findings.evidence: Every other theorem in `F4/RootString.lean` (lines 29–123) is `f4SimplyConnectedRootDatum.<general lemma> f4Length f4Length_mul_pairing_comm ...`; the new proof (lines 131–154) uses only `f4Length_of_root_eq_add_zsmul`, `P.chainBotCoeff_eq_zero_iff` (Mathlib `Chain.lean:309`, general over `RootPairing ι R M N` with `[P.IsCrystallographic]`), and `f4Length_eq_one_or_eq_two`.
findings.fix: Add `RootPairing.chainBotCoeff_eq_zero_of_add_eq_short (length) (hsym) (α β γ) (hlength : ∀ δ, length δ = 1 ∨ length δ = 2) (hβ : length β = 1) (hγ : length γ = 1) (h : P.root γ = P.root β + P.root α) : P.chainBotCoeff α β = 0` in `InvariantForm/RootString.lean` (section with `[Finite I] [P.IsCrystallographic]`), and make the F₄ theorem a one-line application with `f4Length`, `f4Length_mul_pairing_comm`, `f4Length_eq_one_or_eq_two`.
findings.issue: `f4_chainBotCoeff_eq_zero_of_add_eq_short` is proved directly on the pinned F₄ datum, but its proof uses only `length_of_root_eq_add_zsmul`, `chainBotCoeff_eq_zero_iff`, and the {1,2} length dichotomy — exactly the ingredients of the general lemmas it sits next to (`chainBotCoeff_eq_one_of_short_add_short_eq_long`, `exists_short_midpoint_of_long_add_two_short`), all of which are stated for `RootPairing I ℤ M N` in `InvariantForm/RootString.lean` and then specialized to F₄.

findings.evidence: grep: `f4Root_eq_add_zsmul_of_f4KillingRoot_eq_add_zsmul` has no uses outside its definition; `f4Root_eq_add_of_f4KillingRoot_eq_add` is used once (`ModularLattice.lean` bracket closure). The two proof bodies (lines 120–165 and 167–215) differ only by `(n : ℚ) •` and `map_smul`.
findings.fix: State `f4KillingRoot_eq_add_zsmul_iff (α β γ) (n : ℤ) : (f4KillingRoot γ : H → ℚ) = f4KillingRoot β + (n : ℚ) • f4KillingRoot α ↔ f4SimplyConnectedRootDatum.root γ = f4SimplyConnectedRootDatum.root β + n • f4SimplyConnectedRootDatum.root α`, and obtain the `n = 1` form used in `ModularLattice.lean` by `simpa using (… 1).mp h` instead of a separate proof.
findings.issue: `f4Root_eq_add_of_f4KillingRoot_eq_add` is the `n = 1` case of `f4Root_eq_add_zsmul_of_f4KillingRoot_eq_add_zsmul` (line 167) with the ~40-line proof duplicated verbatim; the general zsmul version is then never used anywhere. Together with `f4KillingRoot_eq_add_zsmul` the natural statement is a single iff.

findings.evidence: Lines 243–261 and 265–285 are the same `sum_eq_single`/`split_ifs`/`Fin.cast_injective` argument, differing only by `Pi.neg_apply, Int.cast_neg, neg_zero`; `f4OppositeRootIndex_castAdd` (line 421) already identifies `Fin.addNat (Fin.castAdd 20 i) 24` with the opposite root.
findings.fix: Prove `f4ModularCoroot_f4OppositeRootIndex (α) : f4ModularCoroot (f4OppositeRootIndex α) = f4ModularCoroot α` (from `coroot (-α) = -coroot α` at the integral level and `CharTwo`/`neg_eq_self` in a `ZMod 2`-module), then obtain `f4ModularCoroot_addNat_castAdd` as `by rw [← f4OppositeRootIndex_castAdd, f4ModularCoroot_f4OppositeRootIndex, f4ModularCoroot_castAdd]`.
findings.issue: `f4ModularCoroot_addNat_castAdd` repeats the entire `Finset.sum_eq_single` proof of `f4ModularCoroot_castAdd` (line 243) for the negated coroot instead of deriving it; the natural statement is that modular coroots are invariant under `f4OppositeRootIndex` (since `-v = v` over `ZMod 2`), from which both the `castAdd` and `addNat` forms follow via `f4OppositeRootIndex_castAdd`.

summary: The core ideal/basis constructions sit at the right level, but one root-string lemma is proved only for the pinned F₄ datum although every sibling in the file is a specialization of a general RootPairing result, and two transport/coroot lemmas duplicate full proofs for special cases of more general statements in the same PR.
